author: Linnaeus, 1758
habitat: 이끼와 선태류로 덮인 건조한 구릉(둥지 자리)
summary: 해마다 봄과 가을에 수천 마리가 국내를 지나가는 나그네새이다. 갑각류, 지렁이, 곤충을 즐겨 먹는다. 이끼와 선태류가 덮인 건조한 구릉의 움푹한 곳에 둥지를 틀고 한배에 알 4개를 낳는다. 구북구 동부와 북극 툰드라, 쿠릴 열도, 팔라우 제도, 일본, 타이완 등에 분포한다.

art.subject: Red Knot (Calidris canutus), adult in breeding plumage as seen on Korean west-coast tidal flats in late April and May: face, supercilium, throat, neck, breast and belly rich brick-red to rufous-orange; crown streaked black and rufous; mantle and scapulars with large black centres and rufous and whitish-grey fringes, giving a mottled black, chestnut and silver look; wing coverts plainer grey; lower belly and undertail coverts white with scattered dark brown spots and chevrons. Bill black; dark eye; legs dull greenish-grey to blackish-olive.
art.pose: standing on wet mud, side view
art.scene: Korean west-coast tidal mudflat at low tide during spring migration in May, shining wet mud with shallow channels; no people, buildings or text
views: adult breeding plumage (late April–May), side view standing: brick-red face, neck, breast and belly, mottled black, chestnut and silver-grey back and scapulars, white lower belly and undertail with dark spots, straight black bill about head length

adult winter plumage, side view standing: plain pale grey upperparts with fine white fringes, whitish supercilium, grey-washed finely streaked breast, white underparts with sparse dark chevrons on the breast sides and flanks

juvenile (August–October), side view standing: grey upperparts in which each feather has a thin dark subterminal line and a white fringe, giving a neat scaly pattern, faint buff wash on the finely streaked breast
art.build: Stocky, plump, medium-sized sandpiper, 23.5cm, about the length of a Common Starling but much bulkier and clearly larger than a Dunlin, with a short neck, round head and short legs; horizontal, solid stance. Bill black, straight and fairly thick at the base, about as long as the head. Legs short, greenish-grey. At rest the wingtips reach about the tail tip. In flight a narrow white wing-bar, a pale grey rump finely barred darker that looks whitish-grey at distance but never pure white, and a plain grey tail.
avoid: Do not paint a long or drooping bill — Great Knot (Calidris tenuirostris) is larger with a longer bill and heavy black breast spots.
Do not give it a pure white rump or a long decurved bill (Curlew Sandpiper).
Do not spread the rufous of the underparts over the upperparts; the back is black-centred with rufous and grey fringes and the wing coverts are grey.
Do not make the legs long or bright yellow; they are short and dull greenish-grey.
